$comment: Options object for the P1 device. Its keys (connector_options/listener_options/controller_options) are spread into P1.__init__ kwargs by main.create_classes — keep in lockstep with the constructor; tests/test_config.py enforces this.

connector_options.$comment: A P1 carries a raw DSMR telegram, and the only transport that can deliver one to this device is 'mqtt' — including a 'pseudo' replay connector declaring emulates: "mqtt", which Config resolves before injecting. Anything else is refused with one ERROR at startup and produces no readings; devices/p1.py's UNSERVABLE_PROTOCOLS names the LoRa transports specifically; everything else falls through to its PROTOCOL_REFUSAL. `protocol` is injected by Config from the connector this device names and must not be written here.

name.$comment: Must reference an existing connector name — enforced by Config at load time, not by the schema

pattern.$comment: The client-side routing regex the connector matches each topic against. Required because it has no default and cannot get one: there is no standard P1-over-MQTT topic — dsmr2mqtt, Tasmota's tele/<name>/SENSOR, HomeWizard and every hand-rolled reader choose their own — so a synthesised default would not fail loudly, it would match a different meter's telegram on the same broker and file its readings under this device's name. A missing one is a load-time warning, never fatal.

subscription.$comment: The MQTT topic filter, distinct from the routing regex above. Optional although MQTTConnector.inject_devices warns when it is absent, because subscriptions are a connector-wide set: a sibling device declaring a broader filter already covers a device that declares only a pattern.

controller_options.$comment: Inert on this kind: a P1 is a meter, is not a Switch, and is_writable is False, so Device.control refuses a command before it reaches the connector. Documented rather than removed so a reader knows the omission is the device's nature and not an oversight.
